newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia unveils draft law on ASX demutualisation.
newsitem.headline: Australia unveils draft law on ASX demutualisation.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday released draft legislation for the demutualisation and public listing of the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX).

"The proposed legislation will facilitate the decision of ASX members to convert from its traditional form as a mutual organisation to a public company limited by shares," said Ian Campbell, the parliamentary secretary to the treasurer.
"The bill will ensure that the proposed change to the ASX's corporate form will not adversely impact on the ASX's regulatory role in the financial marketplace."

The draft legislation limits individual holdings to a maximum five percent and charges the Australian Securities Commission with supervising any decision of the ASX to list istelf on its own exchange.
The ASX plans to demutualise from January 1, 1998.
Exchange members in October approved the demutualisation, in a move which would clear the way for the exchange to become the first publicly-listed stock exchange in the world.
Campbell said the draft legislation was open for public comment until October 22. Copies are available from Treasury.
